output.reason: A 70-year-old on warfarin with head trauma yesterday now reporting a bad headache and two episodes of vomiting requires immediate emergency imaging for possible intracranial hemorrhage.
output.patientMessage: Go to the emergency department now. A head injury while taking warfarin, with a bad headache and vomiting today, can mean bleeding around the brain that needs an urgent CT scan. Have someone drive you or call 911 — do not drive yourself. If you become drowsy, confused, weak on one side, have slurred speech or a seizure, call 911 immediately.
differential: Traumatic intracranial hemorrhage (e.g. subdural hematoma) in an anticoagulated patient
